go:357476.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 1
go:357476.question:
​​​​​​The ratio of boys to girls in a class is $7$ to $3$.

Among the options below, an acceptable value for the total number of students in the class is:

  1. $21$
  2. $37$
  3. $50$
  4. $73$

detailed_solution.markdown: Boys : girls = 7 : 3, so the total must be a multiple of 7 + 3 = 10. Only 50 is (35 boys, 15 girls).

go:357475.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 2
go:357475.question:
A polygon is convex if, for every pair of points, $\text{P}$ and $\text{Q}$ belonging to the polygon, the line segment $\text{PQ}$ lies completely inside or on the polygon.

Which one of the following is $\underline{\text{NOT}}$ a convex polygon?

detailed_solution.markdown: Shape (A) has a notch (an inward corner). A segment between two points on either side of the notch passes outside the shape, so it is not convex. The triangle, square and trapezium are convex.

go:357474.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 3
go:357474.question:
Consider the following sentences:

  1. Everybody in the class is prepared for the exam.
  2. Babu invited Danish to his home because he enjoys playing chess.

Which of the following is the $\text{CORRECT}$ observation about the above two sentences?

  1. $\text{(i)}$ is grammatically correct and $\text{(ii)}$ is unambiguous
  2. $\text{(i)}$ is grammatically incorrect and $\text{(ii)}$ is unambiguous
  3. $\text{(i)}$ is grammatically correct and $\text{(ii)}$ is ambiguous
  4. $\text{(i)}$ is grammatically incorrect and $\text{(ii)}$ is ambiguous

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - (i) "Everybody ... is prepared" is grammatically correct ("everybody" takes a singular verb). - (ii) "he" could mean Babu or Danish $\rightarrow$ ambiguous.

go:357473.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 4
go:357473.question: A circular sheet of paper is folded along the lines in the directions shown. The paper, after being punched in the final folded state as shown and unfolded in the reverse order of folding, will look like _______.

detailed_solution.markdown: Unfold in reverse order: - The punch on the vertical fold line opens into a long horizontal slot at the top; unfolding the horizontal fold copies it to the bottom. - The small punch on the horizontal fold line opens into a small vertical slot; unfolding the vertical fold copies it to the other side. - The quarter-circle at the corner becomes a full circle in the centre. This is pattern (A): long horizontal slots top and bottom, small vertical slots left and right.

go:357472.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 5
go:357472.question:
___________ is to surgery as writer is to ___________

Which one of the following options maintains a similar logical relation in the above sentence?

  1. Plan, outline
  2. Hospital, library
  3. Doctor, book
  4. Medicine, grammar

detailed_solution.markdown: A doctor performs surgery; a writer produces a book (person : their work).

go:357471.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 6
go:357471.question:
We have $2$ rectangular sheets of paper, $\text{M}$ and $\text{N}$, of dimensions $\text{6 cm $\times$ 1 cm}$ each. Sheet $\text{M}$ is rolled to form an open cylinder by bringing the short edges of the sheet together. Sheet $\text{N}$ is cut into equal square patches and assembled to form the largest possible closed cube. Assuming the ends of the cylinder are closed, the ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cube is _________.

  1.  $\frac{\pi}{2}$
  2. $\frac{3}{\pi}$
  3. $\frac{9}{\pi}$
  4. $3\pi$

detailed_solution.markdown: Cylinder: short edges (1 cm) joined $\rightarrow$ circumference 6, height 1. $r=\frac{3}{\pi}$, $V=\pi r^2h=\frac{9}{\pi}$. Cube: area 6 cm$^2$ cut into 6 squares of 1 cm$^2$ $\rightarrow$ side 1, V = 1. Ratio $=\frac{9}{\pi}$

go:357470.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 7
go:357470.question:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Items} & \textbf{Cost} & \textbf{Profit %} & \textbf{Marked Price} \\ & \text{(₹)} & & \text{(₹)} \\\hline P &5,400 &---&5,860\\\hline Q&---&25&10,000\\\hline\end{array}$$

Details of prices of two items $P$ and $Q$ are presented in the above table. The ratio of cost of item $P$ to cost of item $Q$ is $3:4$. Discount is calculated as the difference between the marked price and the selling price. The profit percentage is calculated as the ratio of the difference between selling price and cost, to the cost 

$(\text{Profit} \%=\dfrac{\text{Selling price – Cost}}{\text{Cost}} \times 100)$

The discount on item $Q$, as a percentage of its marked price, is _______

  1.  $25$
  2. $12.5$
  3. $10$
  4. $5$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Cost of Q = $5400\times\frac43=7200$.

Selling price of Q = 7200 $\times$ 1.25 = 9000.

Discount = 10000 $-$ 9000 = 1000 = 10% of the marked price.

go:357469.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 8
go:357469.question:
There are five bags each containing identical sets of ten distinct chocolates. One chocolate is picked from each bag.

The probability that at least two chocolates are identical is __________

  1. $0.3024$
  2. $0.4235$
  3. $0.6976$
  4. $0.8125$

detailed_solution.markdown:
P(all 5 different) = $\frac{10\times9\times8\times7\times6}{10^5}=\frac{30240}{100000}=0.3024$

P(at least two identical) = 1 $-$ 0.3024 = 0.6976

go:357468.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 9
go:357468.question:
Given below are two statements $1$ and $2$, and two conclusions $\text{I}$ and $\text{II}$

  • $\text{Statement 1:}$ All bacteria are microorganisms.
  • $\text{Statement 2:}$ All pathogens are microorganisms.
  • $\text{Conclusion I:}$ Some pathogens are bacteria.
  • $\text{Conclusion II:}$ All pathogens are not bacteria.

Based on the above statements and conclusions, which one of the following options is logically $\text{CORRECT}$?

  1. Only conclusion $\text{I}$ is correct
  2. Only conclusion $\text{II}$ is correct
  3. Either conclusion $\text{I}$ or $\text{II}$ is correct
  4. Neither conclusion $\text{I}$ nor $\text{II}$ is correct

detailed_solution.markdown: Both bacteria and pathogens are inside "microorganisms", but nothing says how bacteria and pathogens relate to each other. They may overlap or not, so neither "some pathogens are bacteria" nor "all pathogens are not bacteria" follows. They are also not complementary (both could fail), so "either" is wrong too.

go:357467.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | GA Question: 10
go:357467.question:
Some people suggest anti-obesity measures $\text{(AOM)}$ such as displaying calorie information in restaurant menus. Such measures sidestep addressing the core problems that cause obesity: poverty and income inequality.

Which one of the following statements summarizes the passage?

  1. The proposed $\text{AOM}$ addresses the core problems that cause obesity
  2. If obesity reduces, poverty will naturally reduce, since obesity causes poverty
  3. $\text{AOM}$ are addressing the core problems and are likely to succeed
  4. $\text{AOM}$ are addressing the problem superficially

detailed_solution.markdown: The passage says these measures "sidestep" the core problems (poverty and inequality). So they deal with obesity only on the surface.

go:357451.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 1
go:357451.question:
Suppose that $L_1$ is a regular language and $L_2$ is a context-free language. Which one of the following languages is $\text{NOT}$ necessarily context-free?

  1. $L_1 \cap L_2$
  2. $L_1 \cdot L_2$
  3. $L_1- L_2$
  4. $L_1\cup L_2$

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Computation - Context Free Language
detailed_solution.markdown:
With $L_1$ regular and $L_2$ CFL:

- $L_1\cap L_2$, $L_1\cdot L_2$, $L_1\cup L_2$ are always CFL (closure properties).

- $L_1-L_2=L_1\cap\overline{L_2}$ needs the complement of a CFL, which need not be CFL. E.g. $L_1=\Sigma^*$ gives just $\overline{L_2}$.

go:357450.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 2
go:357450.question:
​​​​​Let $P$ be an array containing $n$ integers. Let $t$ be the lowest upper bound on the number of comparisons of the array elements, required to find the minimum and maximum values in an arbitrary array of $n$ elements. Which one of the following choices is correct?

  1. $t>2n-2$
  2. $t>3\lceil \frac{n}{2}\rceil \text{ and } t\leq 2n-2$
  3. $t>n \text{ and } t\leq 3\lceil \frac{n}{2}\rceil$
  4. $t>\lceil \log_2(n)\rceil \text{ and } t\leq n$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Process elements in pairs: compare the two, then compare the smaller with the current min and the larger with the current max. That is 3 comparisons per 2 elements: about $\lceil3n/2\rceil-2$ comparisons, and this is optimal.

So $t \gt n$ and $t\le3\lceil n/2\rceil$.

go:357449.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 3
go:357449.question:
Consider the following three functions.

$$f_1=10^n\quad f_2=n^{\log n}\quad f_3=n^{\sqrt {n}}$$

Which one of the following options arranges the functions in the increasing order of asymptotic growth rate?

  1. $f_3, f_2, f_1$
  2. $f_2, f_1, f_3$
  3. $f_1, f_2,f_3$
  4. $f_2, f_3, f_1$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Write each as a power of 2:

- $f_2=n^{\log n}=2^{(\log n)^2}$

- $f_3=n^{\sqrt n}=2^{\sqrt n\log n}$

- $f_1=10^n=2^{n\log10}$

Compare exponents: $(\log n)^2 \lt \sqrt n\log n \lt n\log 10$ for large n.

go:357448.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 4
go:357448.question:
Consider the following statements.

  • $S_1:$ The sequence of procedure calls corresponds to a preorder traversal of the activation tree.
  • $S_2:$ The sequence of procedure returns corresponds to a postorder traversal of the activation tree.

Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. $S_1$ is true and $S_2$ is false
  2. $S_1$ is false and $S_2$ is true
  3. $S_1$ is true and $S_2$ is true
  4. $S_1$ is false and $S_2$ is false

detailed_solution.markdown: In an activation tree a procedure is called (visited) before its children $\rightarrow$ calls follow preorder. A procedure returns only after all its children return $\rightarrow$ returns follow postorder.

go:357447.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 5
go:357447.question:
Consider the following statements.

  • $S_1:$ Every $\text{SLR(1)}$ grammar is unambiguous but there are certain unambiguous grammars that are not $\text{SLR(1)}$.
  • $S_2:$ For any context-free grammar, there is a parser that takes at most $O(n^3)$ time to parse a string of length $n$.

Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. $S_1$ is true and $S_2$ is false
  2. $S_1$ is false and $S_2$ is true
  3. $S_1$ is true and $S_2$ is true
  4. $S_1$ is false and $S_2$ is false

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- S1: an SLR(1) table has no conflicts, so every SLR(1) grammar is unambiguous. Some unambiguous grammars (e.g. many LALR/LR(1) grammars) are not SLR(1) $\text{---}$ TRUE.

- S2: the CYK algorithm parses any CFG (in CNF) in $O(n^3)$ $\text{---}$ TRUE.

go:357446.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 6
go:357446.question:
Let the representation of a number in base $3$ be $210$. What is the hexadecimal representation of the number?

  1. $15$
  2. $21$
  3. $\text{D}2$
  4. $528$

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Concept / Subtopic**: Digital Logic & Number Representation - Base Radix Conversion
- **Given Representation**:
  - A number $N$ is represented in base $3$ (ternary) as:
    $$N = (210)_3$$
- **Step-by-Step Analytical Derivation**:
  1. **Convert from Base 3 to Decimal (Base 10)**:
     $$N_{10} = 2 \times 3^2 + 1 \times 3^1 + 0 \times 3^0$$
     $$N_{10} = 2 \times 9 + 1 \times 3 + 0 = 18 + 3 = 21_{10}$$
  2. **Convert from Decimal to Hexadecimal (Base 16)**:
     - Divide $21$ by $16$:
       $$21 = 1 \times 16 + 5$$
     - Quotient = $1$, Remainder = $5$.
     - Reading digits from most to least significant:
       $$N_{16} = (15)_{16}$$
  3. Direct verification:
     $$1 \times 16^1 + 5 \times 16^0 = 16 + 5 = 21_{10}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option A ($15$)**.

go:357445.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 7
go:357445.question:
Let $p$ and $q$ be two propositions. Consider the following two formulae in propositional logic.

  • $S_1: (\neg p\wedge(p\vee q))\rightarrow q$
  • $S_2: q\rightarrow(\neg p\wedge(p\vee q))$

Which one of the following choices is correct?

  1. Both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are tautologies.
  2. $S_1$ is a tautology but $S_2$ is not a tautology
  3. $S_1$ is not a tautology but $S_2$ is a tautology
  4. Neither $S_1$ nor $S_2$ is a tautology

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- S1: $\neg p\wedge(p\vee q)\equiv\neg p\wedge q$, and $(\neg p\wedge q)\rightarrow q$ is always true $\rightarrow$ tautology.

- S2: take p = q = 1: q is true but $\neg p\wedge(p\vee q)$ is false $\rightarrow$ S2 is false $\rightarrow$ not a tautology.

go:357444.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 8
go:357444.question:
Consider the following two statements.

  • $S_1$: Destination $\text{MAC}$ address of an $\text{ARP}$ reply is a broadcast address.
  • $S_2$: Destination $\text{MAC}$ address of an $\text{ARP}$ request is a broadcast address.

Which one of the following choices is correct?

  1. Both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are true
  2. $S_1$ is true and $S_2$ is false
  3. $S_1$ is false and $S_2$ is true
  4. Both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are false

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - ARP request: the sender does not know the MAC, so it is broadcast $\text{---}$ S2 TRUE. - ARP reply: sent directly (unicast) to the requester's MAC $\text{---}$ S1 FALSE.

go:357443.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 9
go:357443.question:
Consider the following array.$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|} \hline 23&32&45&69&72&73&89&97 \\ \hline\end{array}$$ Which algorithm out of the following options uses the least number of comparisons (among the array elements) to sort the above array in ascending order?

  1. Selection sort
  2. Mergesort
  3. Insertion sort
  4. Quicksort using the last element as pivot

detailed_solution.markdown: The array is already sorted. - Insertion sort: each element is compared once with its left neighbour $\rightarrow$ n $-$ 1 = 7 comparisons (best case). - Selection sort always does n(n $-$ 1)/2 = 28. - Merge sort needs more than 7 (about 12 here). - Quicksort with the last element as pivot on sorted input is the worst case (28).

go:357442.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 10
go:357442.question:
A binary search tree $T$ contains $n$ distinct elements. What is the time complexity of picking an element in $T$ that is smaller than the maximum element in $T$?

  1. $\Theta(n\log n)$
  2. $\Theta(n)$
  3. $\Theta(\log n)$
  4. $\Theta (1)$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Look only at the root and its children:

- If the root has a right child, the root is smaller than something, so it is not the maximum $\rightarrow$ pick the root.

- Otherwise the root is the maximum, and its left child is smaller $\rightarrow$ pick the left child.

A constant number of steps $\rightarrow$ $\Theta(1)$.

go:357441.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 11
go:357441.question:
In the context of operating systems, which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to paging?

  1. Paging helps solve the issue of external fragmentation
  2. Page size has no impact on internal fragmentation
  3. Paging incurs memory overheads
  4. Multi-level paging is necessary to support pages of different sizes

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- Any free frame can hold any page, so there is no external fragmentation $\text{---}$ TRUE.

- Larger pages waste more space in the last page (internal fragmentation) $\text{---}$ FALSE.

- Page tables take memory (and TLB, extra accesses) $\text{---}$ TRUE.

- Multi-level paging is used to shrink page tables, not to support different page sizes $\text{---}$ FALSE.

go:357440.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 12
go:357440.question:
Let $\langle M \rangle$ denote an encoding of an automaton $M$. Suppose that $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$. Which of the following languages is/are $\text{NOT}$ recursive?

  1. $L= \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M$ is a $\text{DFA}$ such that $L(M)=\emptyset \}$
  2. $L= \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M$ is a $\text{DFA}$ such that $L(M)=\Sigma^* \}$
  3. $L= \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M$ is a $\text{PDA}$ such that $L(M)=\emptyset \}$
  4. $L= \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M$ is a $\text{PDA}$ such that $L(M)=\Sigma ^* \}$

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Computation - Recursive and Recursively Enumerable Languages
detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - DFA emptiness: check whether a final state is reachable $\rightarrow$ decidable. - DFA universality: complement the DFA and check emptiness $\rightarrow$ decidable. - PDA emptiness: convert to a CFG and check whether S generates any string $\rightarrow$ decidable. - PDA universality ($L=\Sigma^*$): undecidable $\rightarrow$ not recursive.

go:357439.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 13
go:357439.question:
Suppose a database system crashes again while recovering from a previous crash. Assume checkpointing is not done by the database either during the transactions or during recovery.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

  1. The same undo and redo list will be used while recovering again 
  2. The system cannot recover any further
  3. All the transactions that are already undone and redone will not be recovered again 
  4. The database will become inconsistent

detailed_solution.markdown: Without checkpoints, recovery always starts from the log. Undo and redo are idempotent (doing them again gives the same result), so after a second crash the same undo and redo lists are built from the log and applied again. The database can still recover and stays consistent.

go:357438.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 14
go:357438.question:
Which of the following standard $C$ library functions will always invoke a system call when executed from a single-threaded process in a $\text{UNIX/Linux}$ operating system?

  1. $\textsf{exit}$
  2. $\textsf{malloc}$
  3. $\textsf{sleep}$
  4. $\textsf{strlen}$

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - exit: must ask the kernel to end the process $\rightarrow$ always a system call. - sleep: must ask the kernel to suspend the process $\rightarrow$ always a system call. - malloc: often served from already allocated heap memory; calls brk/mmap only sometimes. - strlen: pure user-space computation.

go:357437.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 15
go:357437.question:
Consider a linear list based directory implementation in a file system. Each directory is a list of nodes, where each node contains the file name along with the file metadata, such as the list of pointers to the data blocks. Consider a given directory $\textsf{foo}$.

Which of the following operations will necessarily require a full scan of $\textsf{foo}$ for successful completion?

  1. Creation of a new file in $\textsf{foo}$
  2. Deletion of an existing file from $\textsf{foo}$
  3. Renaming of an existing file in $\textsf{foo}$
  4. Opening of an existing file in $\textsf{foo}$

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - Create: must check that no file with that name already exists $\rightarrow$ scan the whole list. - Rename: must check that the new name is not already used $\rightarrow$ scan the whole list. - Delete / open an existing file: stop as soon as the file is found $\rightarrow$ not necessarily a full scan.

go:357435.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 16
go:357435.question: In an undirected connected planar graph $G$, there are eight vertices and five faces. The number of edges in $G$ is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Euler's formula for a connected planar graph: V $-$ E + F = 2.

8 $-$ E + 5 = 2 $\rightarrow$ E = 11

go:357434.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 17
go:357434.question:
Consider the following undirected graph with edge weights as shown:

The number of minimum-weight spanning trees of the graph is ___________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Take all 0.1 edges first (Kruskal). They form no cycle and split the graph into two trees: the top row (3 vertices) and the bottom 6 vertices.

To join these two parts we need one 0.9 edge; the three vertical edges from the top row down to the middle row all cost 0.9. Any one of them works.

go:357433.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 18
go:357433.question: The lifetime of a component of a certain type is a random variable whose probability density function is exponentially distributed with parameter $2$. For a randomly picked component of this type, the probability that its lifetime exceeds the expected lifetime (rounded to $2$ decimal places) is ____________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Exponential with $\lambda=2$: mean = $\frac1\lambda=\frac12$, and $P(X \gt x)=e^{-\lambda x}$.

$P\left(X \gt \frac12\right)=e^{-2\cdot\frac12}=e^{-1}\approx0.37$

go:357432.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 19
go:357432.question:
There are $6$ jobs with distinct difficulty levels, and $3$ computers with distinct processing speeds. Each job is assigned to a computer such that:

  • The fastest computer gets the toughest job and the slowest computer gets the easiest job.
  • Every computer gets at least one job.

The number of ways in which this can be done is ___________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
The toughest job goes to the fastest and the easiest to the slowest. The other 4 jobs can go to any of the 3 computers: $3^4=81$ ways.

The middle computer must get at least one job; remove the cases where all 4 go to the other two: $2^4=16$.

81 $-$ 16 = 65

go:357431.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 20
go:357431.question: Consider the following expression.$$\displaystyle \lim_{x\rightarrow-3}\frac{\sqrt{2x+22}-4}{x+3}$$The value of the above expression (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ___________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
At x = $-$3 the numerator is $\sqrt{16}-4=0$ (form 0/0). Use L'Hospital:

$\frac{d}{dx}\sqrt{2x+22}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+22}}$ $\rightarrow$ at x = $-$3: $\frac14=0.25$

go:357430.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 21
go:357430.question: Consider the following sequence of operations on an empty stack.$$\textsf{push}(54);\textsf{push}(52);\textsf{pop};\textsf{push}(55);\textsf{push}(62);\textsf{s}=\textsf{pop};$$Consider the following sequence of operations on an empty queue.$$\textsf{enqueue}(21);\textsf{enqueue}(24);\textsf{dequeue};\textsf{enqueue}(28);\textsf{enqueue}(32);\textsf{q}=\textsf{dequeue};$$ The value of $\textsf{s+q}$ is ___________.

detailed_solution.markdown: Stack: push 54, push 52, pop (52), push 55, push 62, pop $\rightarrow$ s = 62. Queue: enqueue 21, 24, dequeue (21), enqueue 28, 32, dequeue $\rightarrow$ q = 24. s + q = 86

go:357429.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 22
go:357429.question:
Consider a computer system with a byte-addressable primary memory of size $2^{32}$ bytes. Assume the computer system has a direct-mapped cache of size $\text{32 KB}$ ($\text{1 KB}$ = $2^{10}$ bytes), and each cache block is of size $64$ bytes.

The size of the tag field is __________ bits.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Lines = 32 KB / 64 B = 512 $\rightarrow$ 9 index bits. Offset = 6 bits.

Tag = 32 $-$ 9 $-$ 6 = 17 bits

go:357428.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 23
go:357428.question:
A relation $r(A, B)$ in a relational database has $1200$ tuples. The attribute $A$ has integer values ranging from $6$ to $20$, and the attribute $B$ has integer values ranging from $1$ to $20$. Assume that the attributes $A$ and $B$ are independently distributed.

The estimated number of tuples in the output of $\sigma _{(A>10)\vee(B=18)}(r)$ is ____________.

detailed_solution.markdown: A takes 15 values (6-20) and B takes 20 values (1-20). The official key accepts two answers, depending on what is counted. Method 1: estimated tuples in the output = 820 - A $\gt$ 10 holds for 11-20, 10 of 15 values $\rightarrow$ $P=\frac23$ - $P(B=18)=\frac1{20}$ - Independent: $P(A \gt 10\vee B=18)=\frac23+\frac1{20}-\frac23\cdot\frac1{20}=\frac{41}{60}$ - Estimated tuples $=1200\times\frac{41}{60}=820$ Method 2: distinct (A, B) value pairs that satisfy the condition = 205 - A $\gt$ 10 with any B: $10\times20=200$ pairs - B = 18 with A $\le$ 10 (A = 6-10): 5 more pairs - Total $=200+5=205$

go:357426.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 25
go:357426.question: Three processes arrive at time zero with $\text{CPU}$ bursts of $16,\;20$ and $10$ milliseconds. If the scheduler has prior knowledge about the length of the $\text{CPU}$ bursts, the minimum achievable average waiting time for these three processes in a non-preemptive scheduler (rounded to nearest integer) is _____________ milliseconds.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Shortest job first minimizes average waiting time. Order 10, 16, 20:

waiting times 0, 10, 26 $\rightarrow$ average = 36 / 3 = 12 ms.

go:357425.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 26
go:357425.question:
​​​Consider the following grammar (that admits a series of declarations, followed by expressions) and the associated syntax directed translation $\text{(SDT)}$ actions, given as pseudo-code

$\begin{array}{lll} P & \rightarrow & D^* E^* \\ D & \rightarrow & \textsf{int ID} \{ \text{record that } \textsf{ID.} \text{lexeme is of type} \textsf{ int\}} \\  D & \rightarrow & \textsf{bool ID} \{ \text{record that } \textsf{ID.} \text{lexeme is of type} \textsf{ bool\}}  \\ E& \rightarrow & E_1 +E_2 \{ \text{check that } E_1. \text{type}=E_2. \text{type} = \textsf{int}; \text{set }  E.\text{type }:= \textsf{int} \} \\ E & \rightarrow & !E_1 \{ \text{check that } E_1. \text{type} = \textsf{bool}; \text{ set } E.\text{type} := \textsf{bool} \} \\ E & \rightarrow & \textsf{ID} \{ \text{set } E. \text{type } := \textsf{int} \} \end{array}$

With respect to the above grammar, which one of the following choices is correct?

  1. The actions can be used to correctly type-check any syntactically correct program
  2. The actions can be used to type-check syntactically correct integer variable declarations and integer expressions
  3. The actions can be used to type-check syntactically correct boolean variable declarations and boolean expressions.
  4. The actions will lead to an infinite loop

detailed_solution.markdown: The rule $E\rightarrow ID$ always sets E.type = int, even when ID was declared bool. So: - Integer declarations and expressions (+) type-check correctly. - Boolean expressions fail: !ID would see an int and report an error. - Nothing loops forever.

go:357424.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 27
go:357424.question:
The following relation records the age of $500$ employees of a company, where $empNo$ (indicating the employee number) is the key:

$$empAge(\underline{empNo},age)$$

Consider the following relational algebra expression:

$$\Pi_{empNo}(empAge \Join_{(age>age1)} \rho_{empNo1,age1}(empAge))$$

What does the above expression generate?

  1. Employee numbers of only those employees whose age is the maximum
  2. Employee numbers of only those employees whose age is more than the age of exactly one other employee
  3. Employee numbers of all employees whose age is not the minimum
  4. Employee numbers of all employees whose age is the minimum

detailed_solution.markdown: The join pairs each employee with every employee who is younger (age $\gt$ age1). An employee appears in the result if at least one other employee is younger, i.e. if their age is not the minimum.

go:357422.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 29
go:357422.question:
Assume that a $12$-bit Hamming codeword consisting of $8$-bit data and $4$ check bits is $d_8d_7d_6d_5c_8d_4d_4d_3d_2c_4d_1c_2c_1$, where the data bits and the check bits are given in the following tables: $$\overset{\textbf{Data bits}}{\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}  \hline  d_{8} & d_{7} & d_{6} & d_{5} & d_{4} & d_{3} & d_{2} & d_{1} \\\hline 1 & 1 & 0 & x & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\\hline \end{array}}\qquad \overset{\textbf{Check bits}}{\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline  c_{8} & c_{4} & c_{2} & c_{1} \\\hline y & 0 & 1 & 0 \\\hline \end{array}}$$ Which one of the following choices gives the correct values of $x$ and $y$?

  1. $x$ is $0$ and $y$ is $0$
  2. $x$ is $0$ and $y$ is $1$
  3. $x$ is $1$ and $y$ is $0$
  4. $x$ is $1$ and $y$ is $1$

detailed_solution.markdown: Positions: 1 c1, 2 c2, 3 d1, 4 c4, 5 d2, 6 d3, 7 d4, 8 c8, 9 d5, 10 d6, 11 d7, 12 d8 (even parity). - c1 checks d1, d2, d4, d5, d7 = 1 + 0 + 0 + x + 1 = x. Given c1 = 0 $\rightarrow$ x = 0. - c8 checks d5, d6, d7, d8 = 0 + 0 + 1 + 1 = 0 $\rightarrow$ y = 0. (c2 and c4 also match: 1 and 0.)

go:357421.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 30
go:357421.question:
Consider the following recurrence relation.

$$T\left ( n \right )=\left\{\begin{array}  {lcl} T(n ∕ 2)+T(2n∕5)+7n & \text{if} \; n>0\\1 & \text{if}\; n=0 \end{array}\right.$$

Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. $T(n)=\Theta (n^{5/2})$
  2. $T(n)=\Theta (n\log n)$
  3. $T(n)=\Theta (n)$
  4. $T(n)=\Theta ((\log n)^{5/2})$

detailed_solution.markdown:
The two subproblems have total size $\frac n2+\frac{2n}{5}=0.9n \lt n$. The work per level shrinks geometrically: $7n,\ 0.9\cdot7n,\ 0.81\cdot7n,\ldots$

Total $=7n(1+0.9+0.81+\cdots)=7n\cdot10=\Theta(n)$

go:357420.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 31
go:357420.question:
Consider the following context-free grammar where the set of terminals is $\{a,b,c,d,f\}$. $$\begin{array}{lll} \text{S} & \rightarrow & d \: a \: \text{T} \mid \text{R} \: f \\ \text{T} & \rightarrow & a \: \text{S} \: \mid \: b \: a \: \text{T} \: \mid \epsilon \\ \text{R} & \rightarrow & c \: a \: \text{T} \: \text{R} \: \mid \epsilon \end{array}$$

The following is a partially-filled $\textsf{LL(1)}$ parsing table.$$\begin{array} {c c c }  & a & b & c & d & f & \$ \\\hline  \text{S} & & & \boxed{1} & \text{S} \rightarrow da \text{T} & \boxed{2} & \\\hline \text{T} & \text{T} \rightarrow a\text{S} & \text{T} \rightarrow ba\text{T} & \boxed{3} &  & \text{T} \rightarrow \varepsilon & \boxed{4}\\\hline \text{R} &  & & \text{R} \rightarrow ca\text{T}\text{R} & &   \text{R} \rightarrow \varepsilon &  \end{array}$$ Which one of the following choices represents the correct combination for the numbered cells in the parsing table (“blank” denotes that the corresponding cell is empty)?

  1. $\boxed{1}\;\text{S} \rightarrow \text{R}f \qquad \boxed{2}\;\text{S} \rightarrow \text{R}f \qquad \boxed{3}\; \text{T} \rightarrow \varepsilon \qquad \boxed{4}\;\text{T} \rightarrow \varepsilon$
  2. $\boxed{1}\;\text{blank} \qquad \boxed{2}\;\text{S} \rightarrow \text{R}f \qquad \boxed{3}\; \text{T} \rightarrow \varepsilon \qquad \boxed{4}\;\text{T} \rightarrow \varepsilon$
  3. $\boxed{1}\;\text{S} \rightarrow \text{R}f  \qquad \boxed{2}\;\text{blank} \qquad \boxed{3}\; \text{blank} \qquad \boxed{4}\;\text{T} \rightarrow \varepsilon$
  4. $\boxed{1}\;\text{blank} \qquad \boxed{2}\;\text{S} \rightarrow \text{R}f \qquad \boxed{3}\; \text{blank} \qquad \boxed{4}\;\text{blank} $

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- $FIRST(Rf)=\{c,f\}$ (R can be $\epsilon$) $\rightarrow$ (1) [S, c] and (2) [S, f] are both $S\rightarrow Rf$.

- $T\rightarrow\epsilon$ goes in FOLLOW(T). T is followed by R in $R\rightarrow caTR$ (gives c, and FOLLOW(R) = {f}), and FOLLOW(T) includes FOLLOW(S) = {$}. So FOLLOW(T) = {c, f, $}.

- (3) [T, c] = $T\rightarrow\epsilon$ and (4) [T, $] = $T\rightarrow\epsilon$.

go:357419.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 32
go:357419.question:
Let $r_i(z)$ and $w_i(z)$ denote read and write operations respectively on a data item $z$ by a transaction $T_i$. Consider the following two schedules.

  • $S_1: r_1(x)r_1(y)r_2(x)r_2(y)w_2(y)w_1(x)$
  • $S_2: r_1(x)r_2(x)r_2(y)w_2(y)r_1(y)w_1(x)$

Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. $S_1$ is conflict serializable, and $S_2$ is not conflict serializable
  2. $S_1$ is not conflict serializable, and $S_2$ is conflict serializable
  3. Both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are conflict serializable
  4. Niether $S_1$ nor $S_2$ is conflict serializable

detailed_solution.markdown: S1: $r_1(y)$ before $w_2(y)$ gives T1 $\rightarrow$ T2; $r_2(x)$ before $w_1(x)$ gives T2 $\rightarrow$ T1. Cycle $\rightarrow$ not conflict serializable. S2: $r_2(x)$ before $w_1(x)$ gives T2 $\rightarrow$ T1; $w_2(y)$ before $r_1(y)$ gives T2 $\rightarrow$ T1. No cycle $\rightarrow$ conflict serializable (T2, T1).

go:357418.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 33
go:357418.question:
Consider the relation $R(P,Q,S,T,X,Y,Z,W)$ with the following functional dependencies.

$$PQ\rightarrow X;\quad P\rightarrow YX;\quad Q\rightarrow Y; \quad Y\rightarrow ZW$$

Consider the decomposition of the relation $R$ into the constituent relations according to the following two decomposition schemes.

  • $D_1:\quad R=[(P,Q,S,T);\;(P,T,X);\;(Q,Y);\;(Y,Z,W)]$
  • $D_2:\quad R=[(P,Q,S);\;(T,X);\;(Q,Y);\;(Y,Z,W)]$

Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. $D_1$ is a lossless decomposition, but $D_2$ is a lossy decomposition
  2. $D_1$ is a lossy decomposition, but $D_2$ is a lossless decomposition
  3. Both $D_1$ and $D_2$ are lossless decompositions
  4. Both $D_1$ and $D_2$ are lossy decompositions

detailed_solution.markdown: D1: join step by step on common attributes that are keys of one side: - (P, Q, S, T) with (P, T, X) on PT: $P\rightarrow X$ so PT $\rightarrow$ X True - with (Q, Y) on Q: $Q\rightarrow Y$ True - with (Y, Z, W) on Y: $Y\rightarrow ZW$ True So D1 is lossless. D2: (T, X) shares no attribute with the other relations, so joining it gives a cross product $\rightarrow$ lossy.

go:357417.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 34
go:357417.question:
Let $G$ be a group of order $6$, and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ such that $1<|H|<6$. Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. Both $G$ and $H$ are always cyclic
  2. $G$ may not be cyclic, but $H$ is always cyclic
  3. $G$ is always cyclic, but $H$ may not be cyclic
  4. Both $G$ and $H$ may not be cyclic

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- G can be the non-abelian group $S_3$ (order 6), which is not cyclic.

- By Lagrange, |H| divides 6 and is strictly between 1 and 6, so |H| = 2 or 3, which are primes. Every group of prime order is cyclic.

go:357416.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 35
go:357416.question:
Consider the two statements.

  • $S_1:\quad$ There exist random variables $X$ and $Y$ such that $  \left(\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E(X))(Y-\mathbb E(Y))]\right)^2>\textsf{Var}[X]\textsf{Var}[Y]$
  • $S_2:\quad$ For all random variables $X$ and $Y, \textsf{Cov}[X,Y]=\mathbb E  \left[|X-\mathbb E[X]|\;|Y-\mathbb E[Y]|\right ]$

Which one of the following choices is correct?

  1. Both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are true
  2. $S_1$ is true, but $S_2$ is false
  3. $S_1$ is false, but $S_2$ is true
  4. Both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are false

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- S1: the left side is $Cov(X,Y)^2$. By Cauchy-Schwarz, $Cov(X,Y)^2\le Var(X)Var(Y)$ always, so S1 is FALSE.

- S2: the right side is always $\ge0$, but covariance can be negative (e.g. Y = $-$X) $\rightarrow$ FALSE.

go:357415.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 36
go:357415.question:
Let $G=(V, E)$ be an undirected unweighted connected graph. The diameter of $G$ is defined as:

$$\text{diam}(G)=\displaystyle \max_{u,v\in V} \{\text{the length of shortest path between $u$ and $v$}\}$$

Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of $G$.

Define graph $G_2$ on the same set of vertices with adjacency matrix $N$, where 

$$N_{ij}=\left\{\begin{array} {lll} 1 &\text{if}\; M_{ij}>0 \text{ or } P_{ij}>0, \text{ where }P=M^2\\0 &\text{otherwise} \end{array}\right.$$

Which one of the following statements is true?

  1. $\text{diam}(G_2)\leq\lceil \text{diam}(G)/2\rceil$
  2. $\lceil \text{diam}(G)/2\rceil<\text{diam}(G_2)< \text{diam}(G)$
  3. $\text{diam}(G_2) = \text{diam}(G)$
  4. $\text{diam}(G)< \text{diam}(G_2)\leq 2\;  \text{diam}(G)$

detailed_solution.markdown:
$P=M^2$ has $P_{ij} \gt 0$ exactly when there is a path of length 2. So in $G_2$, u and v are adjacent whenever their distance in G is 1 or 2.

A shortest path of length d in G can be covered with $\lceil d/2\rceil$ such jumps, so $diam(G_2)=\lceil diam(G)/2\rceil$.

go:357414.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 37
go:357414.question:
​​​​​Consider the following$\text{ ANSI C}$ program.

#include <stdio.h>
int main
{
    int i, j, count;
    count=0;
    i=0;
    for (j=-3; j<=3; j++)
    {
        if (( j >= 0) && (i++))
            count = count + j;
    }
    count = count +i;
    printf("%d", count);
    return 0;
}

Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. The program will not compile successfully
  2. The program will compile successfully and output $10$ when executed
  3. The program will compile successfully and output $8$ when executed
  4. The program will compile successfully and output $13$ when executed

detailed_solution.concept: Programming in C - Programming In C
detailed_solution.markdown: (The loop runs j = $-$3 to 3; the program compiles.) For j $\lt$ 0, && short-circuits, so i++ does not run. For j $\ge$ 0, i++ returns the old value of i: - j = 0: i++ gives 0 (false), i = 1 - j = 1: gives 1 (true), count = 1, i = 2 - j = 2: count = 3, i = 3 - j = 3: count = 6, i = 4 count = 6 + i = 6 + 4 = 10

go:357413.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 38
go:357413.question:
Consider the following language:

$$L= \{ w \in \{0,1\}^* \mid w \text{ ends with the substring } 011 \}$$

Which one of the following deterministic finite automata accepts $L?$

detailed_solution.markdown: States should remember the longest suffix matching a prefix of 011: q0 (nothing), q1 ("0"), q2 ("01"), q3 ("011", final). From the final state: on 0 $\rightarrow$ q1 (suffix "0"), on 1 $\rightarrow$ q0 (suffix "0111" has no useful part). - (A) and (B) loop on 1 at the final state, accepting 0111 False - (C) goes from the final state to q2 on 1, accepting 01111 False - (D) has exactly the transitions above True

go:357412.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 39
go:357412.question:
For a Turing machine $M$, $\langle M \rangle$ denotes an encoding of $M$. Consider the following two languages.

$$\begin{array}{ll} L_1 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on all inputs} \} \\ L_2 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M\text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on some input} \} \end{array}$$

Which one of the following options is correct?

  1. Both $L_1$ and $L_2$ are decidable
  2. $L_1$ is decidable  and $L_2$ is undecidable
  3. $L_1$ is undecidable  and $L_2$ is decidable
  4. Both $L_1$ and $L_2$ are undecidable

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Computation - Recursive and Recursively Enumerable Languages
detailed_solution.markdown:
In 2021 steps, M can read at most the first 2021 input symbols. So "more than 2021 steps" depends only on inputs of length up to 2021, a finite set.

Simulate M for 2022 steps on each such input; this decides both "on all inputs" (L1) and "on some input" (L2).

go:357411.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 40
go:357411.question:
Define $R_n$ to be the maximum amount earned by cutting a rod of length $n$ meters into one or more pieces of integer length and selling them. For $i>0$, let $p[i]$ denote the selling price of a rod whose length is $i$ meters. Consider the array of prices:

$$\text{p}[1]=1,\text{p}[2]=5,\text{p}[3]=8,\text{p}[4]=9,\text{p}[5]=10,\text{p}[6]=17,\text{p}[7]=18$$Which of the following statements is/are correct about $R_7$?

  1. $R_7=18$
  2. $R_7=19$
  3. $R_7$ is achieved by three different solutions
  4. $R_7$ cannot be achieved by a solution consisting of three pieces

detailed_solution.markdown: Best values: R1 = 1, R2 = 5, R3 = 8, R4 = 10 (2+2), R5 = 13 (2+3), R6 = 17, R7 = 18. R7 = 18 is reached by: - one piece of 7 (18) - 6 + 1 (17 + 1) - 2 + 2 + 3 (5 + 5 + 8) Three different solutions, one of which has three pieces (so option 4 is false).

go:357410.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 41
go:357410.question:
An $articulation$ $point$ in a connected graph is a vertex such that removing the vertex and its incident edges disconnects the graph into two or more connected components.

Let $T$ be a $\text{DFS}$ tree obtained by doing $\text{DFS}$ in a connected undirected graph $G$.

Which of the following options is/are correct?

  1. Root of $T$ can never be an articulation point in $G$.
  2. Root of $T$ is an articulation point in $G$ if and only if it has $2$ or more children.
  3. A leaf of $T$ can be an articulation point in $G$.
  4. If $u$ is an articulation point in $G$ such that $x$ is an ancestor of $u$ in $T$ and $y$ is a descendent of $u$ in $T$, then all paths from $x$ to $y$ in $G$ must pass through $u$.

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - The root is an articulation point exactly when it has two or more DFS children: there are no cross edges in an undirected DFS, so its subtrees connect only through the root $\text{---}$ TRUE (option 1 is FALSE). - A leaf of T: removing it leaves the rest of T connected $\rightarrow$ never an articulation point $\text{---}$ FALSE. - Option 4: y's subtree may have a back edge to an ancestor above u (u is an articulation point because of another subtree), giving a path from x to y that avoids u $\text{---}$ FALSE.

go:357409.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 42
go:357409.question:
Consider the following Boolean expression.

$F=(X+Y+Z)(\overline X +Y)(\overline Y +Z)$

Which of the following Boolean expressions is/are equivalent to $\overline F$ (complement of $F$)?

  1. $(\overline X +\overline Y +\overline Z)(X+\overline Y)(Y+\overline Z)$
  2. $X\overline Y + \overline Z$
  3. $(X+\overline Z)(\overline Y +\overline Z)$
  4. $X\overline Y +Y\overline Z + \overline X\; \overline Y \;\overline Z$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Find where F = 1 (XYZ): X = 1 forces Y = 1 (second factor), Y = 1 forces Z = 1 (third), and 000 fails the first. So $F=\Sigma(1,3,7)$ and $\overline F=\Sigma(0,2,4,5,6)$.

- $X\bar Y+\bar Z$ = {4, 5} $\cup$ {0, 2, 4, 6} = {0, 2, 4, 5, 6} True

- $(X+\bar Z)(\bar Y+\bar Z)$ = {0, 2, 4, 5, 6} True

- $X\bar Y+Y\bar Z+\bar X\bar Y\bar Z$ = {4, 5} $\cup$ {2, 6} $\cup$ {0} True

- Option 1 is the dual, not the complement (it contains 1, not 0) False

go:357408.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 43
go:357408.question:
A relation $R$ is said to be circular if $a\text{R}b$ and $b\text{R}c$ together imply $c\text{R}a$.

Which of the following options is/are correct?

  1. If a relation $S$ is reflexive and symmetric, then $S$ is an equivalence relation.
  2. If a relation $S$ is circular and symmetric, then $S$ is an equivalence relation.
  3. If a relation $S$ is reflexive and circular, then $S$ is an equivalence relation.
  4. If a relation $S$ is transitive and circular, then $S$ is an equivalence relation.

detailed_solution.markdown: Reflexive + circular gives an equivalence relation: - Symmetric: aRb and bRb (reflexive) $\Rightarrow$ bRa (circular). - Transitive: aRb and bRc $\Rightarrow$ cRa (circular) $\Rightarrow$ aRc (symmetric). The others fail: reflexive + symmetric need not be transitive; circular + symmetric need not be reflexive (e.g. the empty relation); transitive + circular need not be reflexive either.

go:357407.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 44
go:357407.question:
A $\text{TCP}$ server application is programmed to listen on port number $P$ on host $S$. A $\text{TCP}$ client is connected to the $\text{TCP}$ server over the network.

Consider that while the $\text{TCP}$ connection was active, the server machine $S$ crashed and rebooted. Assume that the client does not use the $\text{TCP}$ keepalive timer. Which of the following behaviors is/are possible?

  1. If the client was waiting to receive a packet, it may wait indefinitely
  2. The $\text{TCP}$ server application on $S$ can listen on $P$ after reboot
  3. If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a $\text{RST}$ segment
  4. If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a $\text{FIN}$ segment

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - The client gets no notice of the crash; without keepalive, a client waiting to receive may wait forever $\text{---}$ possible. - After reboot the application can bind and listen on port P again $\text{---}$ possible. - The rebooted server has no record of the old connection, so a segment from the client gets a RST $\text{---}$ possible. - FIN is sent only on a normal close of a known connection $\text{---}$ not possible.

go:357406.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 45
go:357406.question:
Consider two hosts $P$ and $Q$ connected through a router $R$. The maximum transfer unit $\text{(MTU)}$ value of the link between $P$ and $R$ is $1500$ bytes, and between $R$ and $Q$ is $820$ bytes.

A $\text{TCP}$ segment of size $1400$ bytes was transferred from $P$ to $Q$ through $R$, with $\text{IP}$ identification value as $\textsf{0x1234}.$ Assume that the $\text{IP}$ header size is $20$ bytes. Further, the packet is allowed to be fragmented, i.e., $\textsf{Don’t Fragment (DF)}$ flag in the $\text{IP}$ header is $\textit{not}$ set by $P$.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

  1. Two fragments are created at $R$ and the $\text{IP}$ datagram size carrying the second fragment is $620$ bytes.
  2. If the second fragment is lost, $R$ will resend the fragment with the $\text{IP}$ identification value $\textsf{0x1234}.$
  3. If the second fragment is lost, $P$ is required to resend the whole $\text{TCP}$ segment.
  4. $\text{TCP}$ destination port can be determined by analysing $\textit{only}$ the second fragment.

detailed_solution.markdown: P $\rightarrow$ R: 1400 + 20 = 1420 $\le$ 1500, no fragmentation. R $\rightarrow$ Q (MTU 820): max data 800 (a multiple of 8). - Fragments: 800 and 600 bytes of data $\rightarrow$ datagrams of 820 and 620 bytes $\text{---}$ TRUE. - Routers do not keep or resend fragments $\text{---}$ FALSE. - IP cannot rebuild the datagram without the lost piece; TCP at P must resend the whole segment $\text{---}$ TRUE. - The TCP header (with ports) is only in the first fragment $\text{---}$ FALSE.

go:357405.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 46
go:357405.question:
Consider the following pseudocode, where $\textsf{S}$ is a semaphore initialized to $5$ in line $\#2$ and $\textsf{counter}$ is a shared variable initialized to $0$ in line $\#1$. Assume that the increment operation in line $\#7$ is $\textit{not}$ atomic.

1.  int counter = 0;
2.  Semaphore S = init(5);
3.  void parop(void)
4.  {
5.         wait(S);
6.         wait(S);
7.         counter++;
8.         signal(S);
9.         signal(S);
10.  }

If five threads execute the function $\textsf{parop}$ concurrently, which of the following program behavior(s) is/are possible?

  1. The value of $\textsf{counter}$ is $5$ after all the threads successfully complete the execution of $\textsf{parop}$
  2. The value of $\textsf{counter}$ is $1$ after all the threads successfully complete the execution of $\textsf{parop}$
  3. The value of $\textsf{counter}$ is $0$ after all the threads successfully complete the execution of $\textsf{parop}$
  4. There is a deadlock involving all the threads

detailed_solution.markdown: Each thread needs 2 of the 5 permits, so up to 2 threads can be inside together, and counter++ is not atomic. - 5: threads run one after another $\text{---}$ possible. - 1: thread A reads 0 and is preempted; the others run one by one in the second slot (counter = 4); A writes 1 $\text{---}$ possible. - 0: at least the last write stores a value $\ge1$ $\text{---}$ impossible. - Deadlock: all 5 threads do their first wait (S = 0) and then all block on the second $\text{---}$ possible.

go:357404.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 47
go:357404.question:
Consider a $\textit{dynamic}$ hashing approach for $4$-bit integer keys:

  1. There is a main hash table of size $4$.
  2. The $2$ least significant bits of a key is used to index into the main hash table.
  3. Initially, the main hash table entries are empty.
  4. Thereafter, when more keys are hashed into it, to resolve collisions, the set of all keys corresponding to a main hash table entry is organized as a binary tree that grows on demand.
  5. First, the $3^{\text{rd}}$ least significant bit is used to divide the keys into left and right subtrees.
  6. To resolve more collisions, each node of the binary tree is further sub-divided into left and right subtrees based on the $4^{\text{th}}$ least significant bit.
  7. A split is done only if it is needed, i.e., only when there is a collision.

Consider the following state of the hash table.

Which of the following sequences of key insertions can cause the above state of the hash table (assume the keys are in decimal notation)?

  1. $5,9,4,13,10,7$
  2. $9,5,10,6,7,1$
  3. $10,9,6,7,5,13$
  4. $9,5,13,6,10,14$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Read the state: index 00 empty; 01 has 3 keys (one with 3rd bit 0, two with 3rd bit 1, split by the 4th bit); 10 has 2 keys (3rd bit 0 and 1); 11 has 1 key.

Option C: 10, 9, 6, 7, 5, 13

- 10 = 1010 $\rightarrow$ 10, bit3 = 0; 6 = 0110 $\rightarrow$ 10, bit3 = 1 True

- 9 = 1001 $\rightarrow$ 01, bit3 = 0; 5 = 0101 and 13 = 1101 $\rightarrow$ 01, bit3 = 1, split by bit4 (0 and 1) True

- 7 = 0111 $\rightarrow$ 11 True

The others fail: (A) has 4 $\rightarrow$ index 00; (B) has 1 and 9 colliding with bit3 = 0; (D) has 6 and 14 colliding and nothing in 11.

go:357403.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 48
go:357403.question:
Consider the following $\text{ANSI C}$ function:

int SimpleFunction(int Y, int n, int x)
{
    int total = Y[0], loopIndex;
    for (loopIndex=1; loopIndex<=n-1; loopIndex++)
        total=x*total +Y[loopIndex];
    return total;
}

Let $\textsf{Z}$ be an array of $10$ elements with $\textsf{Z}[i]=1$, for all $i$ such that $0 \leq i \leq 9$. The value returned by $\textsf{SimpleFunction(Z},10,2)$ is __________

detailed_solution.markdown:
The function is Horner's rule: it evaluates $Y[0]x^{n-1}+\cdots+Y[n-1]$.

With all Y[i] = 1, x = 2, n = 10: $2^9+2^8+\cdots+1=2^{10}-1=1023$

go:357402.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 49
go:357402.question:
Consider the sliding window flow-control protocol operating between a sender and a receiver over a full-duplex error-free link. Assume the following:

  • The time taken for processing the data frame by the receiver is negligible.
  • The time taken for processing the acknowledgement frame by the sender is negligible.
  • The sender has infinite number of frames available for transmission.
  • The size of the data frame is $2,000$ bits and the size of the acknowledgement frame is $10$ bits.
  • The link data rate in each direction is $1$ Mbps ($=10^6$ bits per second).
  • One way propagation delay of the link is $100$ milliseconds.

The minimum value of the sender's window size in terms of the number of frames, (rounded to the nearest  integer)  needed  to achieve a link utilization of $50\%$ is_____________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- Frame transmission time = 2000 / $10^6$ = 2 ms

- ACK transmission time = 10 / $10^6$ = 0.01 ms

- Cycle = 2 + 100 + 0.01 + 100 = 202.01 ms

Utilization $=\frac{W\times2}{202.01}=0.5\Rightarrow W=50.5$ $\rightarrow$ about 51 frames.

go:357401.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 50
go:357401.question:
Consider the following $C$ code segment:

a = b + c;
e = a + 1;
d = b + c;
f = d + 1;
g = e + f;

In a compiler, this code segment is represented internally as a directed acyclic graph $\text{(DAG)}$. The number of nodes in the $\text{DAG}$ is _____________

detailed_solution.markdown:
Common sub-expressions share nodes:

- leaves: b, c, 1 (3 nodes)

- b + c (shared by a and d) $\rightarrow$ 1 node

- (b + c) + 1 (shared by e and f) $\rightarrow$ 1 node

- e + f $\rightarrow$ 1 node

Total = 6

go:357400.question:
In a  pushdown automaton $P=(Q, \Sigma, \Gamma, \delta, q_0, F)$, a transition of the form,

where $p,q \in Q$, $a \in \Sigma \cup \{ \epsilon \}$, and $X,Y \in \Gamma \cup \{ \epsilon \}$, represents $$(q,Y) \in \delta(p,a,X). $$Consider the following pushdown automaton over the input alphabet $\Sigma = \{a,b\}$ and stack alphabet $\Gamma = \{ \#, A\}$.

The number of strings of length $100$ accepted by the above pushdown automaton is ___________

detailed_solution.markdown: The PDA pushes # and then an A for every a; in q2 every b pops an A. It can reach the final state q3 only if an A is still on top. So it accepts $a^mb^n$ with $n \lt m$. go:357399.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 52
go:357399.question: Consider the following matrix.$$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\\ 1& 0& 1 & 1\\ 1& 1 & 0 & 1 \\1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$$The largest eigenvalue of the above matrix is __________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
The matrix is $J-I$, where J is the 4 $\times$ 4 all-ones matrix.

Eigenvalues of J: 4, 0, 0, 0. Subtracting 1: 3, $-$1, $-$1, $-$1.

Largest = 3

go:357398.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 53
go:357398.question:
A five-stage pipeline has stage delays of $150, 120, 150, 160$ and $140$ nanoseconds. The registers that are used between the pipeline stages have a delay of $5$ nanoseconds each.
The total time to execute $100$ independent instructions on this pipeline, assuming there are no pipeline stalls, is _______ nanoseconds.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Clock cycle = slowest stage + register delay = 160 + 5 = 165 ns.

Cycles for 100 instructions on 5 stages = 5 + 100 $-$ 1 = 104.

Time = 104 $\times$ 165 = 17160 ns

go:357396.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 54
go:357396.question:
A sender $(\textsf{S})$ transmits a signal, which can be one of the two kinds: $H$ and $L$ with probabilities $0.1$ and $0.9$ respectively, to a receiver $(\textsf{R})$.

In the graph below, the weight of edge $(u,v)$ is the probability of receiving $v$ when $u$ is transmitted, where $u,v \in \{H,L\}$. For example, the probability that the received signal is $L$ given the transmitted signal was $H$, is $0.7$.

If the received signal is $H,$ the probability that the transmitted signal was $H$ (rounded to $2$ decimal places) is __________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
From the graph: P(recv H | sent H) = 0.3 and P(recv H | sent L) = 0.8.

P(recv H) = 0.1 $\times$ 0.3 + 0.9 $\times$ 0.8 = 0.03 + 0.72 = 0.75

Bayes: $P(\text{sent H}\mid\text{recv H})=\frac{0.03}{0.75}=0.04$

go:357397.title: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 | Question: 55
go:357397.question:
Consider the following instruction sequence where registers $\text{R1}, \text{R2}$ and $\text{R3}$ are general purpose and $\text{MEMORY[X]}$ denotes the content at the memory location $\text{X}.$

$\begin{array}{llc} \textbf{Instruction} & \textbf{Semantics} & \textbf{Instruction Size} \text{ (bytes)} \\ \hline \text{MOV } \text{R1}, (5000) & \text{R1} \leftarrow \text{MEMORY}[5000] & 4 \\ \hline \text{MOV } \text{R2}, (\text{R3}) & \text{R2} \leftarrow \text{MEMORY[R3]} & 4 \\ \hline \text{ADD} \text{R2}, \text{R1} & \text{R2} \leftarrow \text{R1} + \text{R2} & 2 \\ \hline \text{MOV } (\text{R3}), \text{R2} & \text{MEMORY[R3]} \leftarrow \text{R2} & 4 \\ \hline \text{INC } \text{R3} & \text{R3} \leftarrow \text{R3}+1  & 2 \\ \hline \text{DEC } \text{R1} & \text{R1} \leftarrow \text{R1}-1 & 2 \\ \hline \text{BNZ } 1004 & \text{Branch if not zero to the} & 2 \\ & \text{given absolute address}& \\ \hline \text{HALT}  & \text{Stop} & 1 \\ \hline \end{array}$

Assume that the content of the memory location $5000$ is $10$, and the content of the register $\text{R3}$ is $3000$. The content of each of the memory locations from $3000$ to $3020$ is $50$. The instruction sequence starts from the memory location $1000$. All the numbers are in decimal format. Assume that the memory is byte addressable.

After the execution of the program, the content of memory location $3010$ is ____________

detailed_solution.markdown:
R1 = MEMORY[5000] = 10, so the loop (BNZ back to 1004) runs 10 times. Each pass adds R1 to MEMORY[R3] and moves R3 one byte ahead.

R3 goes 3000, 3001, $\ldots$, 3009. Location 3010 is never written, so it keeps its value 50.
